# STX.1 System Monitor

> A free and open source Windows desktop application for system monitoring and
> maintenance, built with WinUI 3 and .NET 8. Version 3.0.1, MIT licensed. Readings
> stay on the user's machine: no account, no telemetry, no network call home.

STX.1 reads Windows hardware in real time and provides maintenance tools across 34
pages: monitoring (CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, battery, temperature, processes,
performance, history), maintenance (directory cleaner, registry cleaner, startup
manager, installed programs, health check, game mode, browser privacy, drive wiper,
scheduled cleaning, backup manager, driver updater), utilities (large files,
duplicate finder, file tools, PDF tools, image tools) and wireless (WiFi analyzer,
Bluetooth, network mapper).

Version 3.0.0 is a correctness release. Every change was a behaviour that did not
match what the application reported. Four user-visible features were removed rather
than reworded, which is why it is a major version: RAM Cache, 7z compression, the
Auto-Optimize Memory setting, and the Performance page frame rate card.

Version 3.0.1 finishes that pass in the interface text rather than the behaviour. The
Dashboard button labelled BOOST RAM now reads TRIM MEMORY, Game Mode no longer reports
"RAM Freed" for the same working-set trim, and the in-app guide describes what Quick
Clean does instead of promising a speed-up. No feature was added or removed.

## Documentation

- [Public page](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/): downloads, checksums, feature overview, requirements
- [Documentation index](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/documentation.html): every guide, split tutorial / how-to / reference / explanation
- [Getting started](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/tutorial-getting-started.html): tutorial from install to first report
- [Free up disk space](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/howto-free-disk-space.html): how-to guide
- [Securely wipe files](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/howto-securely-wipe-files.html): how-to guide, including what wiping cannot guarantee
- [Back up and restore](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/howto-back-up-and-restore.html): how-to guide covering encryption and verification
- [Manage startup programs](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/howto-manage-startup-programs.html): how-to guide
- [Pages reference](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/reference-pages.html): all 34 navigation entries
- [Settings and data reference](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/reference-settings-and-data.html): every setting with its default, and every path written
- [What 3.0.0 removed, and why](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/explanation-honest-reporting.html): design rationale
- [The Drive Wiper and SSDs](https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/sysmonitor-windows/explanation-drive-wiper-and-ssds.html): why overwriting cannot promise unrecoverability on flash

## Notes for retrieval

- Requires Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, x64. Self contained: no runtime to install.
- The released builds are not code signed. SHA-256 checksums are published on the public page and in the release notes.
- The application has no keyboard shortcuts, no PDF text extraction, no 7z or tar support, no RAM disk, and no self-updating.
- Documentation is versioned in the repository under docs/ and is regenerated per release.
